key_insight: Task-adaptive fusion of multimodal MRI improved brain tumor segmentation while preserving shared and modality-specific information.
clinical_relevance: The approach may support imaging-based tumor assessment when MRI inputs are incomplete, but this study does not evaluate cancer drug discovery or clinical outcomes.
method: Fuse modality-specific latent distributions using a Wasserstein barycenter.
Learn modality weights jointly with the task objective.
Retain modality-specific information through multilevel decoding and learnable modality embeddings.
evidence_signal: On BraTS 2018, mean Dice scores across all 15 modality combinations were 62.31% for enhancing tumor, 78.83% for tumor core, and 87.30% for whole tumor; separate normative-modeling evaluations used UK Biobank and ADNI.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish prospective clinical performance or generalization across imaging sites and protocols.
paper_title: Task-Adaptive Wasserstein Barycentric Fusion for Multimodal Medical Imaging
